name: Where Is My Mind
memo: Pixies - Where Is My Mind?: surfy clean-ish guitar with spring reverb, light grit and a little chorus. Informed approximation.

band.style_feel: slow half-time pulse, kick on 1, snare on 3, steady hi-hat; loud-quiet dynamics
parts: Part A: intro - the two-note arpeggio guitar line, very sparse drums
Part B: verse - bass and drums enter, steady groove
Part C: chorus ("With your feet on the air and your head on the ground") - fuller band
Part D: solo/instrumental break - full band
Part E: outro - repeat of the intro line and fade
band.tips: Sources list about 162-164 BPM, but the song feels like roughly 82 BPM in half-time, so choose a slow style and check the Trio+ tempo against the record. Key and tempo came from secondary sources; confirm by ear. Play the intro line cleanly for 2 bars before the Trio+ starts learning.

whammy.tuning: Standard (E A D G B E)
how: Leave the Whammy DT off; play in standard tuning.
whammy.tips: No pitch effect or alternate tuning was found for this recording.

originals.guitar: 1970s Gibson Les Paul Goldtop reissue (pickup covers removed)

guitar.position: bridge pickup for the arpeggio line, tone around 7-8
guitar.tone_notes: Santiago's Les Paul is his signature guitar, but one source says the surfy sound on Surfer Rosa may come from overdubbed Jazzmaster/Telecaster parts. Single-coils suit this tone well; with humbuckers, roll the treble up a bit.
